name: AnyPS5
description: Tool for automatic PS5 executables porting to Linux and Windows
one_liner: Converts PlayStation 5 game programs so they can run on an ordinary Windows or Linux computer, without needing a PS5 or an emulator.
buyer: Honestly, nobody who could pay for this legitimately. It's a hobbyist research/preservation tool in a legal gray zone around console game ports; there's no clean commercial buyer here.
business_use_cases: A game-preservation researcher studies how a specific title's binary behaves, for archival and compatibility research purposes.
A hobbyist developer studies the shader recompiler and linking techniques for their own non-commercial systems-programming learning project.
A systems engineer references the relinker and prx-library reimplementation approach when designing porting tools for an unrelated, legally clean platform.

money_ideas.idea: None that are defensible: selling access to or 'as a service' hosting of ported PS5 executables would involve copyrighted game binaries without authorization.

steal_this: Don't build a business on this one. If anything, study the relinker and shader-recompiler engineering techniques and apply them to a platform you actually have rights to port for.
